approachQuestion.prompt:
Count quiet ledger intervals

Input: an integer array changes containing positive, negative or zero adjustments. Return the number of nonempty contiguous intervals whose total adjustment is zero. Distinct endpoint pairs count separately, including overlapping intervals.

Example 1: changes = [2,−2,0]. Output: 3: [0..1], [0..2] and [2..2]. Example 2: changes = [0,0]. Output: 3. Example 3: changes = []. Output: 0. 0 ≤ n ≤ 200,000; −1,000,000 ≤ changes[i] ≤ 1,000,000. Prefix totals and answer fit signed 64-bit integers.

Constraints: input is immutable; all identifiers and numeric entries are signed 32-bit integers unless specified. Arithmetic uses signed 64-bit integers. Prefer the least expected running-time growth, then avoid unnecessary asymptotic auxiliary storage. Non-adversarial hashing of fixed-size integer keys/tuples has expected amortized constant cost.

options.text: Scan a running prefix total, with frequency 1 initially stored for total zero before the array. For each new total, add its prior frequency to the answer, then increment that frequency.
options.feedback: Each prior equal total defines one nonempty zero-sum interval ending here. Counting before inserting excludes the empty interval at this boundary.

options.text: Store all n+1 prefix totals including the initial zero, comparison-sort the copy, and sum c(c−1)/2 over equal-total run lengths c.
options.feedback: Every pair of equal prefix totals gives exactly one interval, so this is correct; ordering all prefixes adds removable work.

options.text: Keep only a set of prior prefix totals and add one on a membership hit.
options.feedback: For [0,0], the second boundary has two prior zero totals and creates two intervals, not one. Membership loses multiplicity.

options.text: Insert the current prefix total before adding its stored frequency to the answer.
options.feedback: For [5], this counts the current prefix against itself and reports an interval although no nonempty zero-sum interval exists.

feedback.reason: Count all earlier occurrences of a repeated prefix state instead of keeping just one boundary.
details: Use a scalar running total and a map of frequencies of previous prefix totals, initialized with 0→1. For every adjustment, update the scalar total, add its current map frequency to a 64-bit answer, then increment that map entry. Do not build an array of prefix totals.
For [0,0], the last boundary has two earlier equal totals and creates two new intervals. A presence set loses that multiplicity; inserting the current prefix first would also count an empty interval.

For each new total, add its prior frequency to the answer, then increment that frequency.”: Each prior equal total defines one nonempty zero-sum interval ending here. Counting before inserting excludes the empty interval at this boundary.

“Keep only a set of prior prefix totals and add one on a membership hit.”: For [0,0], the second boundary has two prior zero totals and creates two intervals, not one. Membership loses multiplicity.

“Insert the current prefix total before adding its stored frequency to the answer.”: For [5], this counts the current prefix against itself and reports an interval although no nonempty zero-sum interval exists.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Count quiet ledger intervals — analyzed method”, n is array length and p is the number of distinct prefix totals including the initial zero, so p≤n+1. Choose its time and auxiliary-space pair. Use the tightest standard bound for the worst legal input for the stated size parameters, with expected time over non-adversarial hashing. Fixed-width integer and fixed-size tuple hash operations take expected amortized O(1); arithmetic, comparison and copying one integer take O(1). Auxiliary space excludes the supplied input and returned result, includes all maps, sets, temporary copies and call stacks. The method is iterative, with constant call-stack space.

feedback.reason: One frequency update per prefix counts intervals without enumerating endpoints.
details: Count all earlier occurrences of a repeated prefix state instead of keeping just one boundary.
Each of n entries generates constant arithmetic and a constant number of expected amortized map operations; expected O(n+1). The number of valid intervals does not change the scan cost.
O(p+1) for one count per distinct prefix total and scalars, including the initial zero total. Neither input nor prefix totals are copied.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(p + 1) auxiliary space.”: Correct under the stated expected/amortized hashing model.
“Expected O(n² + 1) time; O(p + 1) space.”: A numeric count can be quadratic, but each step adds its number of matching boundaries without enumerating intervals.
“Expected O(n + 1) time; O(1) space.”: There may be p distinct prefix totals to count.
“O(n log n + 1) time; O(n + 1) space.”: The fixed method does not sort a prefix array; it updates a frequency map.
